title: नेपालको सन्दर्भमा वर्णव्यवस्थाको समाजशास्त्रीय विश्लेषण
nepali: वर्णव्यवस्था हिन्दु उपमहाद्वीपको चारवर्ण (ब्राह्मण, क्षेत्री, बैश्य, शूद्र) सँग सम्बन्धित छ । यस अध्ययनमा नेपालका खस आर्य, नेवार र मैथिली गरी तीन साँस्कृतिक/भौगोलिक समुदायमा वर्ण व्यवस्था कसरी विस्तार भएको छ भनी व्याख्या गरिएको छ । यो अध्ययन पुस्तकालय विधिबाट गरिएको छ  । पुस्तकालयमा उपलब्ध लेख रचनाको विषयवस्तुलाई यस अध्ययनको तथ्याङ्कको रूपमा प्रयोग गरिएको छ । यसरी अध्ययन गर्दा समाजशास्त्रीय दृष्टिले जातीय व्यवस्था, परम्रागत रूपमा स्थापित नभई खास ऐतिहासिक सन्दर्भमा यसको थालनी भएको र त्यसका खास कारणहरू रहेको देखिन्छ । सोही आधारमा वर्णव्यवस्था स्थापित हुँदै आएको छ भन्ने कुराको व्याख्या गरिएको छ । वर्ण तथा जातजातिका विसङ्गति जहाँबाट जताबाट पसे पनि समाजमा यसको प्रभाव कम भएको अनुभूति हुन्छ । सामाजिक विकाशको नियमित प्रक्रियामा जन्ममा आधारित जात व्यवस्थाका तमाम दुर्गुण हिजो भन्दा आज निकै कम भएका छन् ।
american_english: The caste system is associated with the four varnas (Brahman, Kshatri, Baishi, and Shudra) of the Hindu subcontinent. This study explains how the caste system expands in Nepal's three cultural/geographical communities - Khas (Aryan), Newar and Maithili. This study was done through a library method. The article and compositions available in the library are used as data for this study. So when studied from a sociological perspective, ethnic divisions, which are not established in traditional form but have special historical context, and the special causes behind them are evident. Based on that, it is explained that the caste system is established as it comes. Ethnic and caste disconnections from where they came to where they went have less impact in society. The negative aspects of birth-based ethnic divisions, which are regular processes of social development, are much less today than in the past.

informal_english: The caste system ties in with the four classes (Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras) from the Hindu subcontinent. This research explores how this system spreads across Nepal's three main cultural groups - the Khas (Aryan), Newar, and Maithili people. The study used library research methods, drawing on articles and writings available in libraries for data. When looked at from a social science angle, these ethnic groups weren't traditionally set up, but they have unique historical backgrounds and reasons for existing. The study shows how the caste system naturally developed and spread. Even when ethnic and caste groups moved from their original places to new areas, their differences didn't have as big of an impact on society. The bad parts of being born into a specific caste - which is a normal part of social development - are much less problematic today than they were in the past.
